key_insight: Verifiable AI acceleration must target workload-specific proof costs, which shift with the proof system and input length rather than following a single universal bottleneck.
engineering_relevance: Hardware selection should account for memory capacity, instruction issue and synchronization limits—not just bandwidth or isolated cryptographic speedups.
method: Link AI workloads, proof systems, cryptographic kernels and hardware in a four-layer framework.
Review prior research and measure six provers and seven kernels.
Assess GPUs, reconfigurable logic, custom chips and existing AI accelerators against observed bottlenecks.
evidence_signal: Across input lengths of 64–2048, fixed-weight commitment-opening costs stayed nearly constant while intermediate-value work grew; a 13B-parameter fine-tuning configuration exceeded 40 GB GPU capacity but completed on an 80 GB device.
watch_item: Kernel-level speedups alone do not establish end-to-end gains; validate the complete proof workload and its memory requirements.
paper_title: Infrastructure for Verifiable AI: Where Proof Costs Go and How Hardware Can Help
